# AI Gateway v0.3.0

Verified OIDC access tokens can now use preprovisioned directory users, current
policy and stable ownership across refresh. The default legacy JWT mode remains
compatible; operators opt in after provisioning.

## Changes

- Bind issuer, subject and application audience to an immutable internal user;
  use one stable JWT credential for quotas, ownership, cache and billing.
- Enforce active directory membership, organization, model/tool grants, access
  groups, tags, RPM/TPM and explicitly mapped roles on each request.
- Add audited global-admin JWT binding APIs; empty grants deny new principals.
- Reauthorize queued/background executions against current directory policy;
  cancel revoked running work and settle terminal usage under its original owner.
- Provide secret-free Keycloak clients and an OpenWebUI System OAuth profile.
- Require real Keycloak/OpenWebUI/PostgreSQL identity and failure tests in CI.
- Patch the existing brace-expansion dependency without changing direct UI packages.

## Validation

The profile uses pinned Keycloak 26.3.3 and OpenWebUI 0.11.4 images. Tests cover
two users, real authorization code/PKCE and refresh, grants, JSON/SSE, per-user
model cache, files/Conversations, shared quotas/budgets, PostgreSQL attribution,
expiry, signing-key rotation, logout, directory/IdP failure and recovery.
Providers are deterministic HTTP fixtures; cloud/model quality and complete RAG
workflows require separate selected-provider validation.

Go format/vet/tests/race/build, admin UI tests/build/audit, Helm/OpenAPI,
PostgreSQL regressions and container builds are enforced by the release workflow.

## Upgrade

Apply additive PostgreSQL migration 013_jwt_principals.sql, upgrade compatible
Gateway/Auth, provision bindings, then explicitly select directory JWT mode.
Never enable working IdP trust automatically or link users by email. Existing
virtual keys preserve their grant semantics. Existing fingerprint-owned resources
are not migrated automatically; the documented legacy rollback uses a separate
ownership namespace.

Inference access uses the original user OAuth access token, not an ID token,
OpenWebUI local session token or shared connection key. OpenWebUI built-in tools
must be explicitly assigned or disabled for the selected chat scenario.
Expanded admin browser sessions/refresh/logout are a separate follow-up.
